question.worked_solution:
First, we substitute $u={y}^{3}-2.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}y}=3{y}^{2}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u={y}^{2}\,\text{d}y.
$$

Since $u\to \infty $ when $y\to \infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u={y}^{3}-2$ is as follows:

| $y$ | $3$ | $\infty $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $25$ | $\infty $ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{\infty }\frac{5{y}^{2}}{{({y}^{3}-2)}^{2}}\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{25}^{\infty }\frac{5}{{u}^{2}}(\frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{5}{3}{\int }_{25}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{\infty }\frac{5{y}^{2}}{{({y}^{3}-2)}^{2}}\,\text{d}y & =\frac{5}{3}{\int }_{25}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{3}{\int }_{25}^{\infty }{u}^{-2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{3}{lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{25}^{a}{u}^{-2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{3}{lim}_{a\to \infty }[-{u}^{-1}]_{25}^{a} \\  & =-\frac{5}{3}{lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{u}]}_{25}^{a} \\  & =-\frac{5}{3}{lim}_{a\to \infty }(\frac{1}{a}-\frac{1}{25}) \\  & =-\frac{5}{3}(0-\frac{1}{25}) \\  & =\frac{1}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$
